title: surprise-meter
gist: A small world model trained from scratch on a laptop, on nothing but next-frame pixels, and tested the way psychophysics tests a person: a lawful clip against an impossible twin, with observers that know the laws as the yardstick. One of those observers caught a probe that seemed to see more than the model and was putting more light where the ball comes out than the ball has.
summary: Lets anyone watch a world model guess each frame in the browser, break its physics with a finger, and see how surprised it is.

hero_image.alt: A ball goes behind a slab in a small noisy frame, and an outline of where a linear read of the model's state places the hidden ball is drawn over it.

site.blurb: A world model trained on next-frame pixels, tested with matched lawful and impossible clips against observers that know the laws. A probe of its state seemed to keep a hidden ball in view more than twice as long as the model did, until on a frame where both clips share one state it beat an observer told the answer, 0.78 against 0.66. It was putting 1.4 to 1.8 times the ball's light where the ball comes out.
